(1) A STRUCTURAL walk of every JSON under docs/ (139 files parsed at INTEGRATION_SHA) collecting every scalar field whose VALUE is exactly a candidate id - this reports allocation-shaped occurrences ONLY, and is the sweep that decides. (2) A tracked-tree textual sweep via git grep for each candidate id and filename stem. (3) The working-tree directory listing of docs/ops/ods/ and docs/ops/tenancy/. (4) The live Controller's own enumeration, which independently reports v1.0.23 absent.

COLLISION_SWEEP.result_grant_id_W2_24: FREE. HPO-ODS-W2-24 appears NOWHERE as an exact scalar field value in any JSON under docs/. It appears as a textual substring exactly 6 times at INTEGRATION_SHA, and EVERY occurrence is inside a PROHIBITION or cross-reference clause: four in ODS_V1_MAINTENANCE_ADDENDUM_v1.0.22.json (controller_sequencing_rule.controller_33_must_close_before, .enforcement, .no_preallocation, candidate_self_check SC-3) and two in MULTI_ORG_S1_S2_EXECUTION_SCOPE_AUTHORITY_AMENDMENT_v1.0.3.json (CONTROLLER_SEQUENCING.what_controller33_blocks, .no_preallocation).
COLLISION_SWEEP.why_a_textual_grep_alone_would_have_been: RE-REPRODUCED AS A TRAP, not merely inherited from v1.0.22. A bare `git grep 'HPO-ODS-W2-24'` returns SIX hits at INTEGRATION_SHA and would read as a COLLISION, producing a spurious STOP_FOR_LINEAGE_COLLISION and deadlocking S3 behind an id nobody has allocated. The distinction that resolves it is STRUCTURAL: an ALLOCATION is a scalar field whose VALUE IS the id (a .GRANT_ID, a .protected_grant.authorityId, a .lineage_derivation.next_grant_id); a PROHIBITION merely NAMES the id inside prose. The structural walk returned ZERO allocation-shaped occurrences of HPO-ODS-W2-24 while the textual sweep returned six - the two sweeps disagreeing is exactly the signal the structural one exists to produce.
COLLISION_SWEEP.structural_sweep_is_non_vacuous: PROVEN, not asserted. AUDIT_VERB_DISPOSITION.deferred_not_waived: BINDING AND LOAD-BEARING. DEFERRED means the obligation SURVIVES in full and is owed by a named successor node. It is NOT dropped, NOT made optional, and NOT satisfied by S3 doing nothing. An implementation that emits these verbs is out of S3 scope; an authority that forgets them is a failure of this addendum.
AUDIT_VERB_DISPOSITION.measured_reason: The current audit_logs INSERT policy REQUIRES organization membership or super-admin, while these two refusal events arise PRECISELY when membership is absent or revoked. MEASURED at INTEGRATION_SHA, db/baseline/stella_g2_schema.sql:8822: `CREATE POLICY audit_logs_insert_member_or_admin ON public.audit_logs FOR INSERT TO uellix_app WITH CHECK (((actor_user_id = auth.uid()) AND (((organization_id IS NOT NULL) AND (organization_id = ANY (public.current_user_org_ids()))) OR public.current_user_is_super_admin())))`. A subject whose membership in the selected organization is absent or revoked fails `organization_id = ANY (current_user_org_ids())` by definition - the refusal and the un-writability have the SAME cause. The two verbs are therefore mechanically inexpressible under S3's authority, not merely inconvenient.

PROHIBITED_WORKAROUNDS.binding: S3 MUST NOT use any of the following to emit these verbs. Each is a STOP, and each is named because it is the obvious way to make the problem disappear.
list: service-role or any other privileged connection
RLS bypass of any form, including SET ROLE or a BYPASSRLS role
a new or altered audit_logs policy
writing the refusal to a different table to dodge the policy
emitting the verb with a NULL organization_id to sidestep the predicate
PROHIBITED_WORKAROUNDS.why_this_is_stated_positively: The compiled threat model treats an audit-write workaround as a PRIVILEGE ESCALATION surface, not a logging convenience: any of the above would give the refusal path a capability the success path does not have.

AUDIT_VERB_DISPOSITION.successor_node: The separate governed node has ALREADY been compiled independently by LANE CK / CK-R2. This addendum neither re-compiles it nor absorbs it, and allocates no lineage for it.

P5_COVERAGE_DISPOSITION.declared_partial_coverage: This is DECLARED PARTIAL COVERAGE. It is NOT an UNKNOWN finding and it is NOT a PASS laundered from a test that cannot fail.
P5_COVERAGE_DISPOSITION.measured_reason: MEASURED at INTEGRATION_SHA, db/baseline/stella_g2_schema.sql:7071: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX user_single_active_membership ON public.organization_members USING btree (user_id) WHERE ((status)::text = 'active'::text)`. While that partial unique index stands, a subject CANNOT hold two active memberships. A behavioural proof that 'the role comes from the SELECTED membership rather than from some other active membership' therefore has NO second membership to distinguish against - the discriminating fixture is unconstructible, not merely unwritten.
